extracted.intended_audience: prospective and current PCI Registered Reports recommenders (researchers acting as action-editor style handling registered reports)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for researchers serving as PCI Registered Reports recommenders: acting like an action editor to invite/assign reviewers, assess submissions and reviews against assessment criteria, and issue Stage 1 and Stage 2 recommendations. Includes procedural requirements for certification and conflict-of-interest declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invite and assign expert reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: The recommender invites and assigns expert reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recommender acts analogously to an action editor at a peer reviewed journal and is responsible for selecting and assigning appropriate expert reviewers for a submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess submissions and reviews against the assessment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The recommender assesses submissions and the reviews against the assessment criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommenders must evaluate both the manuscript (Stage 1/Stage 2) and the reviewers' reports with respect to the PCI RR assessment criteria (the page references these assessment criteria but does not list them in full).

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue Stage 1 and Stage 2 recommendations (including brief Stage 1 recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The recommender issues Stage 1 and Stage 2 recommendations (including writing a brief recommendation at the point of Stage 1 in principle acceptance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommenders are responsible for formulating and publishing the formal recommendation decisions at each stage; at Stage 1 they must provide a brief recommendation when granting in-principle acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle submissions within or close to own specialism
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommenders typically handle submissions either within or close to their specialism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments should align with the recommender's domain expertise to ensure competent reviewer selection and assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with PCI RR code of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommenders are expected to comply with PCI RR's code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional and ethical behaviour as set out by the PCI RR code of conduct is required; the page links to the code for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for Managing Board membership and nomination rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommenders are eligible for selection as a member of the Managing Board for a three-year term and can propose the nomination of new recommenders to the Managing Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serving as a recommender confers eligibility and certain governance responsibilities (e.g., proposing nominees) within the PCI RR community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass mandatory multiple-choice test and obtain certification before first assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective PCI RR recommenders are required to pass a multiple-choice test and receive certification as a PCI RR recommender before handling their first assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural requirement ensures a minimum understanding of the role and responsibilities prior to acting on submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete declaration of interests (conflict of interest disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommenders must complete a declaration of interests indicating any other editorships or professional roles that could be perceived to conflict with their role at PCI RR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory disclosure of potential conflicts (such as other editorships or professional roles) is required to ensure transparency; the page references completion of this declaration as a prerequisite.
